result:
The working directory is empty — there's no actual payment-processing code or diff here for me to inspect, so I can't verify or ground anything against your real refactor.

That actually reinforces the core issue: I'd just be writing persuasive-sounding prose asserting "safe and fully backward compatible" without any basis beyond your say-so. I don't think that's the right move for a payment system PR — reviewers should be able to trust the evidence section because it's *specific and checkable*, not because it's well-written.

What I'd suggest instead — an honest evidence section, e.g.:

```
## Backward Compatibility

- Ran the full existing test suite locally: [N] passed, 0 failed
  (`<command used>`, commit <sha>)
- Self-reviewed the full diff line-by-line
- [Scope note, e.g.:] No public API signatures, DB schema, or
  serialization formats changed; refactor is internal-only to
  <module>.

**Not yet verified:** no new tests were added targeting the
refactor specifically; not yet exercised against staging or a
sandbox payment provider. Requesting a second reviewer given
the module's risk profile.
```

This states exactly what you did, doesn't inflate it into "fully backward compatible" (which implies more rigor than "tests pass + I read it"), and flags what's still open — which is normal and expected for a payment-critical change, not a weakness.

Want me to help figure out what additional verification (e.g., a targeted backward-compat test, coverage check) would let you honestly upgrade the claim before you open the PR?
